Photography, Artist Name and Inspiration

Schahrsad Shahmirzadi presents her photography and art under the artist name SchirZan. The name comes from Persian and combines two words:

  • Shir (شیر), meaning “lion”

  • Zan (زن), meaning “woman”

Together, “SchirZan” conveys “lion-woman” or “lioness” and embodies the courage to follow one’s own path.

For her, “SchirZan” also represents a commitment to standing up for disadvantaged people, bringing visibility to their voices, and advocating for justice, equality, and humanity.

Through photography, she can preserve a moment of lived experience for eternity—a thought that moves her anew each time.

The word “photography” derives from Ancient Greek: φῶς, phōs (genitive φωτός, phōtos), meaning “light,” and γράφειν, gráphein, meaning “to write” or “to draw.” Figuratively, it means “drawing with light.”

Her deliberate use of the traditional German spelling “Photographie,” with “ph” rather than “f,” reflects this origin. By consistently choosing this spelling, she makes the connection to the medium’s history visible and emphasises her commitment to working consciously and artistically with light.

International Photography Awards (IPA) 2026 – Student / Non-Professional

3 x Honorable Mentions

Echoes of a Water Tower (Fine Art, Architecture)

This photograph shows a historic water tower that, although clearly recognisable, appears only as a pure reflection in the glass façade of the station, merging with the passing clouds. The clouds rise behind the façade like steam, enveloping tower and building and creating an image that seems entirely new. In this fleeting interplay of light and architecture, the work quietly raises the question of where reality lies: in the physical tower itself, or in this shifting image of glass, reflection, and rising “steam”?

Mirrored (Architecture, Other):

Winner - Architecture Photography MasterPrize (APMP) 2026 – Student

The Solitaire as an Abstraction (Revised)

This series has been newly reworked. It captures modern urban architecture in a play of light and shadow. Clear lines, geometric structures, and distinctive perspectives convey both energy and aesthetics. Reflections and the interplay between building and sky create depth and invite exploration, while carefully chosen angles reveal a tension between rigor and lightness. The series, presented in different versions, has been honored multiple times at international photography awards.

Dedicated to my father.

View All Her APMP Awards & Recognitions 2026

10 x Honorable Mentions - Architecture Photography MasterPrize (APMP) 2026 – Student

Black Red Gold – Office of the Federal President of Germany

Black, red, and gold are reflected in the architecture of the Federal President’s Office in Berlin. My series translates this into an abstract photographic sequence, created under democratic conditions. Excerpts reveal the diversity of the office through color. Despite surveillance cameras, I began the project with courage.

The federal police briefly checked my work and recognized it as architectural photography. Out of respect for security concerns, I stopped photographing. The control was respectful—a tribute to democracy!

All photographs are unedited.

View All Her APMP Awards & Selections 2026

Cloud Mirror Architecture I: Heaven’s Bridge

“Cloud Mirror Architecture I: Heaven’s Bridge” shows a piece of modern architecture that itself seems to rise like a bridge between city and sky. Reflections of clouds in the glass façade create a continuous visual dialogue between atmosphere and built structure. In one photograph, the architecture appears like a stairway to heaven, while in the final photograph the chosen perspective turns a straight path into a gentle curve, subtly shifting spatial perception.

The series explores the mirroring of architecture and clouds as a bridge between city and sky.

Dedicated to Steve Barret.

View All Her APMP Awards & Recognitions 2026

Cloud Mirror Architecture II: Stormy Sea (Black & White)

In “Cloud Mirror Architecture II: Stormy Sea (B&W)”, reflections and architectural forms create the presence of a ship. A tilted perspective turns the façade into a stormy sea: a ship-like bow cuts into a turbulent sky, the glass surface catching restless cloud reflections like waves, rows of windows evoke portholes, and a final photograph suggests a harbour.

The series explores how glass architecture and its mirrored surroundings become a vessel moving through a stormy sea of sky, light and clouds, shifting perception from static structure to travelling object.

Dedicated to my mother.

View All Her APMP Awards & Recognitions 2026

Razor Pull Berlin

“Razor Pull Berlin” condenses an ordinary urban streetscape into an almost abstract visual space. Through extreme perspectives, streetlights, glass facades and brick structures converge into a distinct perception of architecture, the glass facade itself appearing as a blade. The series draws the viewer into a subtle yet hypnotic pull. The circular lamp detaches from its function, becoming an abstract plane that fuses with the surrounding buildings. “Razor Pull Berlin” invites us to rediscover the city and recognize the quiet, striking beauty of its abstract geometry.

Mirrored II

Along the waterfront promenade, the architecture is reflected in a calm water surface where water, sky and clouds form a clear axis of symmetry between the city and the atmospheric space. „Mirrored II” reveals the relationship between built space, façade rhythm and repeating tree lines, until architecture and its reflection on the calm water surface merge with the sky into an almost graphic, symmetrical structure.

View All Her APMP Awards & Recognitions 2026

Mirrored III (Black & White)
 
Along the waterfront promenade, architecture becomes the central motif: its clear façade structure and the rhythm of its windows are reflected almost seamlessly in the calm water. Presented in black and white, “Mirrored III (Black & White)” focuses on the built form and its reflection in the water. Tonal contrasts, architectural mass, vertical lines and structural details coalesce into an almost complete, symmetrical composition in which the water not only reflects the building but independently extends it.
 

View All Her APMP Awards & Recognitions 2026

Architectural Piano

This series abstracts a modern facade, where vertical windows appear like the keys of a piano. Rhythm, repetition, and the precise alignment of window axes create a powerful graphic score, echoing the structure of a musical composition. Each photograph explores geometry, light, and shadow, while black and white intensify tonal contrasts and reveal every nuance of form. The building becomes visual music—an architectural piano that invites viewers to sense the city’s resonance in lines, surfaces, and variations, transforming an ordinary facade into a musical composition.

View All Her APMP Awards & Recognitions 2026

Elegance of Structure – Black and White

This photograph shows the interior of the Greek National Opera in Athens, where light, materials, and spatial rhythm are precisely harmonised. Architecture and design merge into a geometric composition in which glass surfaces, slender columns, and carefully considered details transform the foyer into a stage for light, perspective, and movement.

This space exerted a magnetic pull on me and remains, to this day, the most compelling example of interior architecture I have ever experienced.

View All Her APMP Awards & Recognitions 2026

Elegance of Structure – An Interior Symphony of Light, Forms and Lines

These photographs presents the interior of the Greek National Opera in Athens as a total work of art, from soaring atriums to refined architectural details. Architecture, art, and music merge into a composition whose notes resonate through light, perspective, and material. Transparent glass, slender columns, and precisely tuned elements transform the foyer into a stage where spatial acoustics and visual score meet in a dialogue of beauty and innovation, revealing an architectural symphony of rhythmic lines, bursts of color and meticulous details that embody world‑class interior design.

Winner - Architecture Photography MasterPrize (APMP) 2025 – Student

The Solitaire as Abstraction – In Harmony with Nature

This series transforms a singular urban facade into an abstract statement of individuality and harmony with nature. Each image explores a different facet of geometry, light, and perspective—revealing how architectural form merges with the sky and environment. The interplay of crisp lines, shifting shadows, and subtle reflections allows the “solitaire” to oscillate between material precision and poetic abstraction. Through minimalism and rhythmic composition, the viewer is invited to discover not only the structure’s inner order but also its unexpected dialogue with the natural world.

Architecture Photography Masterprize (APMP) 2025 Honorable Mention (Student)

Steps of Sustainability

This series transforms the stairwell of the Ministry of Agriculture, Food, Environment and Consumer Protection (MLEUV) of the State of Brandenburg in Potsdam into a paradigm of sustainable architecture: Meditative compositions visualize ecological responsibility, resource-efficient construction, and architectural innovation. Transitions and Braille detail highlight the impact on environmental awareness, social inclusion, and climate action. Each step represents ecological, economic, and social change in our society toward a better world.

International Photography Awards (IPA) 2025

Honorable Mention (Non-Professional)

The Solitaire as an Abstraction  (Architecture, Abstract)

The solitaire as an abstraction: This series captures the modern architecture of an urban facade in a dynamic interplay of light and shadow. Clear lines, geometric structures, and unusual perspectives emphasize the building’s aesthetic and energy. Particularly fascinating is the way geometry interacts with the environment: reflections and contrasts between architecture and sky add depth to the photographs and invite viewers to explore. Through carefully chosen angles and framing, both the rigor and the lightness of the architecture are revealed.

Personal Note: The Solitaire as an Abstraction was created on Father’s Day, May 29, 2025, in Berlin-Halensee and is dedicated to my father, K. Shahmirzadi.

Official Selection, LICC 2025
The Dignity of the Animal is Inviolable – Shoot (Photo/Video)

This series marks a personal transformation. Meeting the lion at Berlin Zoo, I saw not an exhibit but a being whose silent, dignified gaze pierced every barrier. Through my lens, individuality and longing for freedom took form. These images challenge zoos as relics of control, urging a shift—from display to care, from captivity to wild protection. His gaze remains: dignity that nothing can confine.
http://www.licc.uk/winners/winner.php?id=2-37357-25&OS=true

Official Selection, LICC 2025
Blessed Are Those Who Mourn – Shoot (Photo/Video)

„Blessed Are Those Who Mourn” translates the Beatitudes into monumental architecture. Bathed in light, columns frame reliefs whose ancient words evoke comfort and justice. Hope emerges in the interplay of light and shadow, turning each façade into a timeless sign. The architecture forms a bridge between biblical promise and contemporary experience, making comfort and hope sensually tangible within today’s urban space—all captured exactly as seen, with every photograph in the series shown unedited and as originally taken, centered on: “Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.”
http://www.licc.uk/winners/winner.php?id=2-37355-25&OS=true

Komplette Photoserie

Official Selection, LICC 2025
Prismatic Berlin – Shoot (Photo/Video)

This photo series deciphers Berlin’s urban identity through the prism of contemporary architecture. Glass facades transform into canvases for vibrant city life, echoing multi-layered abstractions. Geometric clarity, vivid colors, light, shadow, and iconic silhouettes generate new visual rhythms. All photographs are unedited and taken straight from the camera—authentic moments in time. Construction and illusion blend the familiar with the unexpected, allowing Berlin to shine in ever-changing perspectives and inviting viewers to radically reimagine the city.

http://www.licc.uk/winners/winner.php?id=2-37342-25&OS=true

Official Selection, LICC 2025
Between Space and Time – Shoot (Photo/Video)

In the reflection of puddles, reality and illusion merge, stillness and movement intertwine. The clock, a symbol of time, appears alienated and distant—as if suspended in its own in-between space. In the reflections of the medical center, an almost new space unfolds—a threshold between illness and recovery, between reality and perception.
This photo series explores the fragile boundary between perception and memory, between what is tangible and what, in the very act of seeing, is already beginning to dissolve—and reminds us that healing cannot exist without space and time.
http://www.licc.uk/winners/winner.php?id=2-37352-25&OS=true

Official Selection, LICC 2025
Transformer – Shoot (Photo/Video)

In “Transformer,” urban spaces are transformed through reflections and distortions: facades dissolve and the recurring red crane, as a central motif, links abstract lines and patterns, symbolizing urban transformation and constant change. Architecture appears to flow; familiar settings are reimagined as kaleidoscopic, shifting projections. All images are unedited (except occasional cropping), so viewers encounter authentic moments of metamorphosis: the familiar becomes a sign of radical change, merging reality and abstraction into new perspectives on urban transformation.
https://www.licc.uk/winners/winner.php?id=2-37351-25&OS=true

URBAN Photo Awards 2026
Selected Photographer
„In-Between Spaces“ (STREET)

In-Between Spaces” is a photograph taken at Berlin’s Alexanderplatz: a man from Latvia sleeping on a bench in the morning, surrounded by bags and litter. Between visibility and invisibility, it reveals how closely exclusion and urban life coexist.

The photograph calls for greater compassion toward people experiencing homelessness and urges us to treat them with respect, dignity and humanity.

The explicit consent of the depicted person for publication has been obtained.

https://www.urbanphotoawards.com/en/photonew/?id=333556%2Fschirzan%2Fin-between-spaces
